title: Deliveroo to roll out food delivery robots in the UK
source_used: Business Matters (bmmagazine.co.uk); The Times original paywalled
key_facts: Deliveroo will start pavement robot deliveries of takeaways and groceries in the UK, with the first in London in the coming weeks.
Initial areas: Canary Wharf (east London), Milton Keynes, Leeds, Stockton-on-Tees and Nottingham, where councils permit robot deliveries.
The robots are made by Coco, a US firm with an exclusive deal with Deliveroo; they move at about walking pace using sensors, cameras and AI navigation.
CEO Miki Kuusi said the move is 'not about replacing' riders but a complement; Deliveroo has over 100,000 active UK riders.
Deliveroo is talking to more councils and the Department for Transport about wider permission.
Rival Just Eat uses Starship robots in parts of Britain; campaign group Living Streets called Starship robots a danger to pedestrians in July.
Deliveroo was bought by DoorDash last year for 2.9 billion pounds.
